gloss: all talk; lip service; empty words

definitions.gloss: all talk; lip service; empty words
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who says things but never follows through with action, or statements that are not backed by genuine effort or intention. Always carries a negative, critical nuance.

examples.japanese: あいつは{口|くち}だけだ。
{口|くち}だけじゃなくて、{行動|こうどう}で{示|しめ}してほしい。
examples.english: I want you to show it through actions, not just words.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{約束|やくそく}はいつも{口|くち}だけで{終|お}わる。
examples.english: His promises always end up being nothing but empty words.

examples.japanese: {口|くち}だけの{謝罪|しゃざい}では{許|ゆる}されない。
examples.english: A mere verbal apology won't be forgiven.

notes:
Very common colloquial expression used to criticize someone who talks big but doesn't deliver. Functions as a predicate (口だけだ), a modifier (口だけの人), or part of a larger phrase. The tone is always dismissive or critical.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口|くち}だけの{人|ひと}: person who is all talk
- {口|くち}だけの{約束|やくそく}: empty promise
- {口|くち}だけで{終|お}わる: to end up being just talk
- {口|くち}だけじゃなく: not just words (but action too)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口先|くちさき}だけ: superficial words only — similar meaning, slightly more literary
- {有言不実行|ゆうげんふじっこう}: saying but not doing — four-character compound; formal
- {大口|おおぐち}を{叩|たた}く: to talk big — emphasizes boasting rather than inaction
